newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SAR gov't should focus on land supply - Hang Lung.
newsitem.headline: SAR gov't should focus on land supply - Hang Lung.

text.p: The incoming Hong Kong government should use supply rather than demand measures to contend with Hong Kong's housing problems, Hang Lung Development Ltd chairman Ronnie Chan said on Friday.
"I hope that they will deal with supply rather than deal with demand. If you manage supply then you don't need to manage demand," Chan told reporters.
He said the fact that the government is considering demand-dampening measures "is already an indictment that in our policy we are not doing things appropriately."
Chan pointed out that the commercial property market stabilized after hitting a high in 1993 after the government took action to increase supply.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority warned last month that additional restraints in mortgage lending might be required to cool the territory's real estate market.
On Thursday, Hong Kong director of lands Bob Pope said the supply of flats in Hong Kong will grow next year and increase steadily in the next three years to 2001.
Pope said the provisional forecast for 1998 is for 36,000 units. In 1997, the supply of new flats would be around 20,000, the same yearly increase as in the past two years, he said.
